tip: чтобы (shtoby) plus an infinitive like читать (chitat = to read) means in order to, used when one subject does both actions.
куда бы (kuda by) with ни (ni) means wherever, no matter where; бы sits right after куда and ни before the verb, as in куда бы мы ни поехали.
и (i) repeated before each item means both... and: и красивая, и умная, и добрая (i krasivaya, i umnaya, i dobraya).
несмотря на то что (nesmatrya na to shto) is a fixed phrase for despite the fact that, used before a full clause with a verb like шёл (shyol = was falling).
так (tak) plus что frames so... that: так тихо (tak tiha = so quiet), then что (shto) introduces the result.
две (dve = two) takes the genitive singular, so беда (beda) shifts to беды (bedy) after it, not the plural.
Dates use a neuter ordinal plus the month in the genitive: восьмое марта (vasmoye marta = the eighth of March).
приятно (priyatna = pleasant) takes the dative for whoever feels it: кошке (koshke = to a cat), from кошка (koshka = cat).
The reflexive ending -сь can make a verb passive: строилась (stroilas = was being built), Moscow is not building anything itself.
лучше (luchshe = better) is the irregular comparative of хорошо (harasho = good/well).
с plus the instrumental case means with something: с ушами (s ushami = with ear flaps).
Animate masculine nouns take a genitive-looking accusative object: козла (kazla = goat), not козёл (kazyol).
принято plus an infinitive states a custom with no subject: принято разуваться (prinyata razuvatsya = it's customary to take off shoes).
Russian counts toward the coming hour: половина пятого (palavina pyatava = half of the fifth) is 4:30, halfway to five. пятого is genitive.
